text:
sara (support): FYI BrightArc is reporting 401s immediately after we finished onboarding them. They say the key is present in their dashboard but requests fail. Ticket #9876. Anyone seen this pattern before?

miguel (eng): Can you paste the exact curl they used and the response body? Also which project they're calling (prod vs sandbox)?

sara (support): They sent this:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live_XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Response: 401 Unauthorized: \"invalid_api_key\"
They say the key was created from the onboarding flow (BrightArc - Sandbox) but the frontend is pointing at brightarc-prod.project.redwood.

onboarding-bot: New project created: brightarc-prod (org: BrightArc)

devon (infra): 2 quick checks: 1) Confirm if the key is attached to the same project id as the request path/route. 2) Check if the project has billing/active plan (we sometimes mark keys inactive until billing method added).

josh (cs): I reached BrightArc and they confirmed they clicked the "Create key" from the Sandbox project. They thought keys were global. They also said their engineer copied the prod base-url and didn't switch project.

miguel (eng): That explains the 401 pattern — when a key belongs to a different project/namespace we return 401 with body: 
```json
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "reason": "project_mismatch",
  "detail": "api key exists but is not valid for project 'brightarc-prod'"
}
```

sara (support): Where does that error show up in our logs? I can pull the request id.

miguel (eng): In the runtime logs the auth layer logs: `auth.check -> denied project_mismatch, key_id=sk_live_XXXX, expected_project=brightarc-prod, key_project=sandbox-1`. If you give me the request-id I can show the exact entry.

sara (support): Request-id 01G7Z9Q4T.

miguel (eng): Found it. Entry shows key_project=sandbox-1. Also saw `project_status=suspended` for brightarc-prod due to missing billing method. billing-bot: Payment method required for project brightarc-prod; provisioning keys disabled. :warning:

kate (solutions): Two remediation paths: 1) Create a new API key under the brightarc-prod project and have them rotate to it (recommended). 2) If they prefer using sandbox key, update their client base URL to the sandbox project endpoint (not ideal for production). Also if billing was the blocker we can advise their billing contact to add a card and then re-enable provisioning.

sara (support): I asked the customer to create a new key in the prod project. They said they don't see the prod project in their UI (maybe because it's pending billing).

josh (cs): I just DM'd their admin to add a billing method. They added a card.

billing-bot: Billing method added by user: brad@brightarc.com. Project brightarc-prod is now active.

sara (support): OK I regenerated a key in brightarc-prod and sent it to their eng.

brightarc-eng (via josh): Confirmed — rotated to new key and calls succeed. 200 OK, embeddings returned. Thanks! :tada:

miguel (eng): Quick note for internal docs: we should add a short checklist for onboarding support: (1) verify key_project == request_project, (2) check project_status (active/suspended), (3) confirm header format (Authorization: Bearer <key>), (4) advise key rotation rather than moving keys between projects.

sara (support): Adding that to the onboarding playbook now. Also leaving instructions in ticket #9876 that fix was: create key under brightarc-prod after billing update and rotate.

kate (solutions): Filed a tiny follow-up GH issue for the docs: onboarding -> project-key-mismatch checklist.

miguel (eng): Optional: we could add a clearer 401 message text for project_mismatch that tells customers "check project/billing or rotate key" so support sees less of these. I'll open an RFC.

sara (support): Closing thread once ticket updated. Thanks all. :heart:
